message.content:
**Most Famous Sculpture of the 19th Century**

> **“Liberty Enlightening the World” – the Statue of Liberty**  
> *(Unveiled 28‑July‑1886)*  

While technically a public monument, the Statue of Liberty is essentially a colossal marble‑bronze sculpture created by Frédéric Augustus Bourgeois (the design) and completed under the direction of Alexandre Gustave Eiffel’s engineering team. Its iconography—an allegorical female figure holding a torch above her head while she carries a tablet inscribed “JULY IV MDCCLXXVI”—has become synonymous with liberty, democracy, and international goodwill. Because of this universal symbolism—and because it has been photographed, reproduced, and referenced countless times across media—the Statue of Liberty stands out as the single most recognizable work of sculpture produced in the nineteenth century.

---

### Why it eclipses all others

| Feature | Statue of Liberty |
|---------|-------------------|
| **Global reach** | Seen in virtually every major city around the world through replicas, postcards, films, and digital renderings. |
| **Cultural impact** | Symbol of American immigration (“Welcome aboard!”); used in political speeches, protests, and celebrations worldwide. |
| **Longevity & preservation** | Continues to attract millions of visitors each year; maintained by dedicated conservation programs. |
| **Iconic imagery** | Torch held aloft, broken chains below feet, tablet bearing the Declaration of Independence—all instantly identifiable. |

Other highly celebrated 19th‑century sculptures certainly exist—such as:
* *Rosa Bonheur’s “Horse Fair”* (1858)
* *François Rude’s “Marianne” / “La Marseillaise”* (1829–30)
* *Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss”* (1889)

…but none match the Statue of Liberty’s combination of artistic merit, historical context, and enduring visual presence.

---

#### Quick Reference

| Year | Artist(s) | Title | Location |
|------|-----------|-------|----------|
| 1886 | Frédéric Bourgeois + Gustave Eiffel | Statue of Liberty | New York Harbor, USA |
| 1889 | Auguste Rodin | The Kiss | Musée d’Orsay, Paris |
| 1830 | François Rude | La Marseillaise | Place du Panthéon, Paris |
| 1858 | Rosa Bonheur | Horse Fair | Louvre Museum, Paris |

If you’re interested in exploring how the Statue of Liberty compares to other masterpieces—or in learning about specific techniques used in its construction—just let me know!
